info.title: FM Quantizer Firmware — Technical Documentation
info.subtitle: C++ / PlatformIO reimplementation for the Arduino Nano (ATmega328P)

legalnotice.para: Licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later, the same terms as the original firmware.

abstract.para: This document describes the architecture, modules, persistence format and user-facing features of the FM Quantizer firmware. The firmware is a deterministic, hardware-independent core wired to a thin AVR hardware abstraction layer, which makes the entire signal and UI logic testable on a development host.

section.title: Overview
section.para: The FM Quantizer is a two-channel Eurorack module that rounds an incoming v/oct control voltage to the nearest note of a user-defined scale. Each channel supports transposition before and after quantization, a scale-degree shift, portamento (glide), a trigger-driven delay, and a choice of track-and-hold, sample-and-hold or continuous quantization. The two channels can run independently or be linked to share one configuration.

This implementation is a clean reimplementation of the original Rust firmware rather than a mechanical port. The behaviour was reproduced from an analysis of the original, several defects were corrected, and new features were added (see ).

section.title: Architecture
section.para: The firmware is split into three layers with a strict dependency direction: the core depends only on the abstract HAL interfaces, and the concrete AVR layer depends on both. Nothing in the core includes an Arduino or AVR header, so it compiles and runs on a host.

listitem.para: All signal processing, the menu state machine, LED frame encoding and the persistence logic. Pure C++ with no platform dependencies; fully unit-tested.

Small pure-virtual interfaces: IClock (millisecond and microsecond monotonic time), IDigitalOutput, IDigitalInput, ISpiBus, IEeprom and IAnalogInputs. The core is written against these, and tests provide fakes.
Arduino-backed implementations of the HAL interfaces plus the two SPI chip drivers (Mcp4922Dac and Tlc5947LedDriver). One file per hardware element.
Instantiates the objects, restores state, plays the startup animation and runs the 1 kHz processing loop.

section.title: Core modules
section.para: Each core module is a single responsibility with a speaking name and a documented public interface.

row.entry: Fixed-point pitch types (Q8.8 semitones, Q8.24 glide) and shared constants.
ADC→semitone and semitone→DAC conversions (exact integer relationships).
Nearest-note search and scale-degree stepping within a scale.
Two-channel engine: hysteresis, shifts, sample/track-and-hold, delay and glide.
UI state machine: scale editing, sub-menus, save/load, erase and the brightness-calibration mode.
Decodes the twelve note buttons from a single ADC ladder and emits press/hold/release events.
Colour model and encoding of a 12-LED frame into the 36-byte TLC5947 shift order (with the panel's physical rotation).
Red/green brightness steps (1–12) and their mapping to 12-bit PWM levels.
Pure time→frame function for the power-on ring animation.
CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE used to protect every persisted record.
Fixed-layout encoding/decoding of channel configs and full state.
Slot-based scale/config storage and the wear-levelled "last state" ring.

section.title: Signal path

step.para: The CV input is read by the ADC (0–1023) and converted to a Q8.8 semitone value: semitones = adc × 30, which maps the full ADC range onto ten octaves exactly.
Pre-shift (whole semitones) is applied, then the value is quantized to the nearest selected scale note with hysteresis to prevent flicker at note boundaries.
Sample-and-hold (on trigger edge) or track-and-hold selects when a new value is latched; an optional delay defers the output by a number of samples.
Glide integrates the output toward its target for portamento. The result is converted to a 12-bit DAC code with round-to-nearest.

section.para: Channel B may operate in absolute mode (its own input) or relative mode (its input added to channel A's). The loop runs at 1 kHz, so the sample counts used for delay and trigger widths correspond to milliseconds.

section.title: Persistence format
section.para: The ATmega328P has 1 KiB of internal EEPROM. Every record is framed with a start marker and a trailing CRC-16 so a corrupt or partially written record is detected and ignored rather than trusted.

seglistitem.seg: 6 bytes each: marker, version, 12-bit note mask, CRC-16.
36 bytes each: marker, version, 32-byte serialized full configuration, CRC-16. The payload includes Quantizer state, both Arpeggiators, selected channel and UI layer.
12 slots of 42 bytes: marker, 32-bit sequence number, version, 32-byte full configuration, 2-byte brightness calibration, CRC-16.

section.para: The live state is written round-robin across the ring, each write carrying a monotonically increasing sequence number. On load, the valid slot with the highest sequence number wins; if none is valid, safe defaults are used. This spreads erase/write wear across the ring and guarantees that a power loss mid-write cannot corrupt the previously good state. Writes use the EEPROM's update semantics (a cell is only physically written when its value changes), and the working configuration is mirrored to the ring only a few seconds after the last change, further reducing wear.

The exact byte offsets and sizes are defined in PersistenceLayout and checked at compile time with static_assert, so any change to the serialized structures that would overflow a region fails the build rather than silently corrupting memory.

section.title: Power-on behaviour
section.para: At power-on a single amber dot travels once around the twelve LEDs as a self-test, then the last saved channel A/B configuration and LED calibration are restored.

section.title: LED brightness calibration mode
section.para: Red and green brightness can be set independently so amber and the two primaries look balanced on the builder's specific LEDs.

listitem.para: Enter: hold Shift + Load + Save together for five seconds; the LEDs blink to confirm.
Adjust: the twelve note buttons pick a brightness level (1–12, clockwise) for the selected colour; all LEDs preview it live.
Switch colour: Shift + A selects green (channel A), Shift + B selects red (channel B).
Save: hold Shift alone for five seconds; the ring blinks three times and normal operation resumes.

section.title: Corrections and additions relative to the original

listitem.para: Fixed a bit-vector clear that never turned a bit off.
Replaced a glide-integrator assertion (a potential hang) with clamping.
Removed an inline-assembly workaround that depended on undefined behaviour.
Pitch→DAC conversion rounds to the nearest code instead of truncating.
Corrected the 1 kHz timer reload for an exact sample rate.
Added the startup ring animation, automatic state restore, CRC-protected and wear-levelled storage, and the brightness-calibration mode.

section.title: Building and testing
section.para: The project uses PlatformIO. Three environments are defined: nanoatmega328new (default) and nanoatmega328 for the two Nano bootloader variants, and native for the host unit tests.
section.programlisting: pio run -e nanoatmega328new # build firmware pio run -e nanoatmega328new -t upload # flash pio test -e native # run unit tests
section.para: The host test suite exercises the whole core: pitch and scale math, the quantizer, CRC, persistence (including wear-levelling and corruption detection), the debouncer and long-press logic, the full menu state machine including the calibration flow, and the startup animation. The thin AVR glue in src/ is compiled by the firmware build and verified on hardware.
